newsitem.title: UK: Fixed income arbitrage works for hedge funds in Q3.
newsitem.headline: Fixed income arbitrage works for hedge funds in Q3.

text.p: Fund consultants TASS Management Ltd said fixed income arbitrage and special situations strategies gave the best gains for the third quarter 1996 of all the hedge fund categories they track.

TASS said in a statement that on average, fixed income arbitrage funds returned 3.33 percent, with special situations returning 3.19 percent on the quarter. The group tracks 1,600 alternative investment managers and funds globally. The leading categories for the first nine months of the year were emerging markets funds with average returns of 23.9 percent, followed by European equity funds with 18.1 percent.

TASS chief executive Nicola Meaden said strong global bond markets, especially in Europe, had fuelled the performance of fixed income arbitrage players while "great opportunities in US distressed and special situations propelled that cetgory".

"For the first nine months of the year, runups in the Russian, Eastern European and Latin American markets benefited emerging markets funds," she added. "Corporate restructurings in the markets of developed European countries were responsible for the strong showing of the European equity funds."
The third best performing category for both Q3 and the first nine months of the year was US equity funds, up an average 2.35 percent on the quarter and 15.3 percent to end-Q3.
The worst performing hedge fund categories for Q3 were global macro, down an average of 1.17 percent, followed by short sellers down an average of 0.38 percent.
Commodity Trading Advisors (CTAs) lost an average of 0.69 percent for Q3 and were down 0.25 percent to end-Q3.
Those managers with dedicated currency strategies listed an average return of 4.56 percent for the quarter and 0.48 percent to end Q-3, TASS said.
